Message to U.S. Citizens:
Demonstration Alert: Rally in Rizal Park, Manila near the U.S. Embassy
https://t.co/Q5ZGOYHtDI

Location: Rizal Park and Roxas Boulevard
Event: Iglesia ni Cristo rally, November 16-18, 2025

The religious organization Iglesia ni Cristo will hold a three-day rally in Rizal Park in Manila November 16-18, 2025. Local authorities expect large crowds. The City of Manila has suspended in-person classes in all public and private schools in Manila on November 17 and 18 in anticipation of the event.

Visitors to the area should expect heavy traffic and road closures around Rizal Park and nearby areas, including the immediate vicinity of the U.S. embassy. Due to the embassy’s close proximity to the rally site and the expectation of heavy traffic congestion and security in the immediate vicinity of the embassy, we are suspending public services on Monday, November 17.

Actions to Take:
- U.S. citizens should avoid the rally.  Foreign nationals found engaging in a protest or mass demonstration could be considered in violation of their immigration status, as stated in Operation Order SMB-2015-026 (https://t.co/XLsQRz7O10).
- Follow local media and government sources for updates on possible disruptions and for traffic re-rerouting schemes due to the event.
- Exercise caution when in the vicinity of any large gatherings.  Follow instructions from local authorities.
———————————————————

For further information and assistance:
- Enroll in the Smart Traveler Enrollment Program (https://t.co/q8w0nZfWZo) to receive Alerts and make it easier to locate you in an emergency.
- Contact the U.S. Embassy in Manila, Philippines, located at 1201 Roxas Boulevard, at +(63) (2) 5301-2000, from 7:30 a.m. to 4:30 p.m. Monday through Friday. After-hours emergency number for U.S. citizens is +(63) (2) 5301-2000.
- Call 1-888-407-4747 toll-free in the United States and Canada or 1-202-501-4444 from other countries from 8:00 a.m. to 8:00 p.m. Eastern Standard Time, Monday through Friday (except U.S. federal holidays).
- See the State Department’s travel website (https://t.co/Tiyt8sq7F9) for the Worldwide Caution, Travel Advisories, Alerts, and the Philippines Country Specific Information (https://t.co/ApMa3LxNZy).

data.text:
Following the accusations made by former Ako Bicol party-list representative Zaldy Co, Malacañang expressed doubt on Friday that the upcoming three-day protest action of the Iglesia Ni Cristo would spark outrage against the Marcos administration.

During a press briefing, Palace Press Officer Undersecretary Atty. Claire Castro was asked how concerned is President Ferdinand ''Bongbong'' Marcos Jr. with the INC rally given that Co made claims against him.

The INC earlier said its rally at the Quirino Grandstand in Manila from Nov. 16 to 18 aims to call for accountability for corruption in alleged flood control projects.
